  copy instead — the value always arrives.
- Sending a received frame back unmodified moves no data at all: it crosses
  as a reference to the region it arrived from.
  This holds through polars or pyarrow (`pl.from_arrow(f)`, `pa.table(f)`)
  as long as no column was modified.
- Modifying some columns moves only those columns.
  Each unmodified column still crosses as a reference, so a relay that adds
  one computed column pays for one column.
  R reads the unmodified columns as views of the original region.
- A polars or pyarrow object that wraps a received frame keeps the frame's
  shared-memory region alive until it is deleted and garbage-collected.
  Holding many of them at once can force later sends back to copying, so
  delete them when they are no longer needed.

## Dates, times, and other types

- A factor crosses as `list[str | None]` on its own, or as a
  dictionary-encoded column inside a frame.
- A `Date` crosses as `datetime64[D]` or Arrow `date32`.
  A `POSIXct` crosses as a naive `datetime64[us]` or `timestamp[us, tz]`:
  microsecond precision, `NaT` read as `NA`.
  A named timezone is kept as frame column metadata but dropped from a
  standalone vector.
  Naive Python datetimes arrive in R with `tzone = "UTC"`.
- A `difftime` crosses as `timedelta64[us]`: microsecond precision, `NA`
  read as `NaT`.
  R's five units cross by value; a round trip normalizes them to seconds.
  `timedelta64` arrays of any non-calendar unit cross likewise (numpy
  scalars and `datetime.timedelta` included).
  Inside a frame, a difftime column exports to Arrow as `duration[us]`,
  and an Arrow `duration` column arrives as a difftime.
- A `POSIXlt`, Arrow
  `date64`/`time`/`interval`, and ordered dictionaries (polars
  Enums) are declined at send time.
- An R vector with `names` is declined (numpy has no per-element names).
  A matrix crosses with values exact — the data is never transposed.
  `dimnames` and character matrices are declined.
- Cross-language sends copy R's ALTREP vectors by value: exact values, the
  compact representation is not preserved.

## The dtype matrix

The exact correspondence between Python and R dtypes.
Conversion happens once, at send time.
The identity rows (float64, int32, int64, complex128, uint8) are a plain
memcpy.

| Python sends | R receives | Notes |
|----|----|----|
| `bytes` / uint8 | raw | Arrow uint8 with nulls: `TypeError` (R raw has no NA) |
| int8 / int16 / uint16 | integer | widened, exact |
| int32 | integer | |
| uint32 | double | widened, exact |
| int64 | integer64 (bit64's layout) | bit-exact; `INT64_MIN` reads as `NA` |
| uint64 | double | exact to ±2^53; past it, `NA` plus one warning |
| float16 / float32 / float64 | double | float16 and float32 widened, exact |
| bool | logical | |
| complex64 / complex128 | complex | (buffer protocol only; Arrow has no standard complex) |
| Arrow bool / numeric with nulls | logical / numeric with `NA` | the validity bitmap is honored, slices included |
| Arrow strings (utf8 / large_utf8 / string_view) | character | a Series arrives as `list[str \| None]`; a column as a frame column |
| Arrow `date32` / `timestamp[u]` | `Date` / `POSIXct` | the zone name rides a frame column's metadata |
| Arrow `duration[u]` | `difftime` (secs) | the unit converts to seconds; the frame column exports back as `duration[us]` |
| timedelta64 (any non-calendar unit) | `difftime` (secs) | `NaT` reads as `NA`; the unit converts to seconds |
| Arrow dictionary-encoded | factor | an ordered dictionary declines (`polars Enum`: cast to `pl.Categorical`) |
| Arrow ChunkedArray / Table / Series | vector / `data.frame` | chunks are concatenated |
| Arrow nested, decimal, time32/64, interval | — | `DeclinedError` at send time |

Missing values:

- R marks missing values with sentinels inside the data: `INT_MIN` for
  integer and logical, `INT64_MIN` for integer64, and a special NaN value
  (`NA_real_`) for double.
  Arrow nulls convert to these sentinels, so R sees correct `NA`s.
- Read from Python, the result depends on the accessor:
  - Copied reads (`list(...)`, `Frame.to_dict()`) give honest dtypes: a
    logical arrives as `bool_` when it has no `NA`, else int32; an integer
    arrives as int32 when `NA`-free, else float64 with NaN (every int32 value
    is exact in float64).
  - Zero-copy views keep the sentinel values in the buffer.
    `.to_numpy()` applies the same rule, reading NA-freeness off the
    region's validity section before any data scan.
  - int64 keeps its dtype in every numpy form and warns when an `NA` is
    detected on a copied read or `.to_numpy()`.
    Use `.to_arrow()` for an NA-honest read.
    A genuine Python `-2^63` value round-trips without a warning.
  - Every Arrow export of a logical is Arrow `bool` with a validity bitmap,
    whatever the path.
    Integer exports are int32 or int64 with a validity bitmap.
- A genuine int32 value of `-2147483648` collides with the `NA` sentinel and
  reads as `NA` in R.
  Likewise an int64 value of `-9223372036854775808` reads as `NA_integer64_`.
  numpy sends stay silent.
  An Arrow int32 send with a validity bitmap warns once.
- Python compute treats `NA_real_` as an ordinary NaN.
  Whether the exact NaN value survives arithmetic is platform-dependent — do
  not rely on it.

Round trips are stable after the first hop, and a pass-through echo is
bit-exact: an untouched received view sent back crosses as a reference to its
region — no data moves — so even the `NA_real_` value survives a relay.
A slice or a dtype view of a received view crosses by value.

| Python sends | R sees | Back in Python | Notes |
|----|----|----|----|
| uint8 | raw | uint8 | exact |
| int8 / int16 / uint16 | integer | int32 | widened, values exact |
| int32 | integer | int32 | exact |
| uint32 | double | float64 | exact |
| int64 | integer64 | int64 | exact |
| uint64, ≤ ±2^53 | double | float64 | dtype lost, values exact |
| uint64, past ±2^53 | `NA` | NaN | lost on the first hop |
| float16 | double | float64 | widened, values exact |
| float32 | double | float64 | widened, values exact |
| float64 | double | float64 | exact |
| bool | logical | `bool_` (int32 with NAs) | dtype lost |
| complex64 / complex128 | complex | complex128 | exact |
| timedelta64 | `difftime` | timedelta64[us] | unit normalizes to us, values exact |

| R sends | Python sees | Back in R | Notes |
|----|----|----|----|
| integer | int32 (float64 with NAs) | integer | exact |
| integer64 (bit64) | int64 (warns on `NA`) | integer64 | exact; a genuine Python `-2^63` arrives as `NA` |
| double | float64 | double | exact |
| raw | uint8 | raw | exact |
| complex | complex128 | complex | exact |
| logical | `bool_` (int32 with NAs) | **integer** | the logical tag is lost on a Python round trip (the values are not); a whole view sent back crosses by reference and stays logical |
| difftime | timedelta64[us] | difftime (secs) | units normalize to seconds, values exact; `NA` crosses as `NaT` |

Between two Python processes — a channel or a pool — the conversions on this
page never run: the identity dtypes cross unchanged and everything else
pickles, so an exact Python-to-Python send of a non-identity dtype needs no
work.
They apply only when the other end runs R.
